# Integrating tom_som_cpp_v0

<!-- GENERATED by tom_specs_clitool generate_som — do not edit by hand. -->

`tom_som_cpp_v0` is the typed TomSpecs object-model facade for C++. It depends on `tom_som_cpp_runtime`. Both are versioned to the TomSpecs **model version** (currently `1.1.0`) — pin to that version so your document reads and writes match the model the facade was generated from.

## Quick start

Build and install `tom_som_cpp_v0` (and `tom_som_cpp_runtime`), then compile against it with `pkg-config`:

```cpp
#include "tom_som_cpp_v0.hpp"

#include <iostream>

int main() {
  // A typed Solution Blueprint over a fresh document. The constructor also runs
  // the instantiation-time model-version check (an empty stamp is editable).
  // RAII: the document is a value that must outlive every facade bound to it;
  // getters return std::string by value, so there is nothing to free.
  som::SpecDocument doc;
  tom_som_v0::D00SolutionBlueprint bp(doc);

  bp.setContent("A platform that unifies our fragmented order systems.");

  tom_som_v0::CurrentLandscape cl = bp.currentLandscape();
  cl.setContent("Three legacy systems with no shared customer record.");

  std::cout << bp.content() << "\n";
  return 0;
}
```

## Dependency routes

### pkg-config (installed)

C++ has no universal package registry. Install the facade and the runtime (runtime first — the facade links against it), then let `pkg-config` supply the compile and link flags:

```bash
make -C ../tom_som_cpp_runtime install
make install
c++ myapp.cpp $(pkg-config --cflags --libs tom_som_cpp_v0) -o myapp
```

The facade `.pc` declares `Requires: tom_som_cpp_runtime`, so a single `pkg-config tom_som_cpp_v0` pulls in the runtime flags too. Both `.pc` files report `Version VERSION`.

### Source tarball (vendored)

Produce versioned source tarballs and vendor them into your build:

```bash
make -C ../tom_som_cpp_runtime dist   # tom_som_cpp_runtime-VERSION.tar.gz
make dist                             # tom_som_cpp_v0-VERSION.tar.gz
```

Unpack both alongside your project and add each `include/` to your include path plus the built libraries to your link line.

### In-tree (monorepo)

When the SOM projects sit alongside your code, build the facade in place; its `Makefile` builds the runtime on demand through a relative `RUNTIME_DIR`:

```bash
make                                  # builds runtime + facade libs
c++ myapp.cpp -Iinclude -I../tom_som_cpp_runtime/include \
   build/libtom_som_cpp_v0.a ../tom_som_cpp_runtime/build/libtom_som_cpp_runtime.a \
   -o myapp
```

## Pinning the version

Both `tom_som_cpp_runtime` and `tom_som_cpp_v0` carry version `1.1.0`, taken from the TomSpecs model version. When you upgrade the model, regenerate and move to the new matching version so the facade and your stored documents stay in step.

## Building from source

Regenerate the facade, then build and package both projects from the workspace (runtime first — the facade builds it on demand through its relative `RUNTIME_DIR`):

```bash
dart run tom_specs_clitool/bin/generate_som.dart
cd tom_som_cpp_runtime && make && make dist
cd ../tom_som_cpp_v0 && make && make dist
```

Each `make` builds the static + shared library and the pkg-config file; each `make dist` writes `build/<name>-<version>.tar.gz`.
